correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the spin-raise expression using the scalar equation R''=(m²−ℓ(ℓ+1))R at the equator; spin lowering changes the sign of the mR' term. Legendre parity gives only the stated zeros, and the Pell recurrence preserves x+y≡1 mod 4 with y even, making every positive resonance admissible after omitting degree one. The 2ℓ+1 Fourier orders are distinct residues; the amplitudes and ordinary-area normalization give the stated Gram eigenvalues and image. A blind polar Wigner solution cannot also have zero first derivative at the regular equator. After subtracting visible modes, row multiplication by z=e^{iMφ} turns the two-column system into (1,z²) at (1,i), and the three-column system into (1,z,z²) at (1,i,−1). Both are nonsingular. The one-order and empty cases are immediate; the d-dimensional old kernel proves the lower bound for complex-linear probes. This applies also to the complete repaired RESULT.md. Frozen verify_spin2.py and VERIFICATION.md were inspected, not executed; the recorded finite Wigner and Pell checks do not verify derivative recovery.
